topics.label: Course Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course structure, and the intended learning outcomes regarding environmental carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Intrinsic Factors, Environmental Exposures, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the foundational causes of cancer by examining how intrinsic biological errors, inherited predispositions, and environmental exposures drive cancer incidence across populations.

topics.label: Infectious Agents in Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how biological pathogens and co-infections contribute to malignancy, focusing on Epstein-Barr virus and Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: DNA Adducts and Metabolic Activation of Mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how chemical carcinogens and radiation induce DNA damage directly or via host xenobiotic metabolic activation.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic drivers of cancer, including chronic inflammatory microenvironments, chemical promoters, and tissue-specific developmental timing.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Testing Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the genomic, epidemiological, and laboratory assay systems used to identify carcinogens and test mutagenic potential.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Analysis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic delivers the closing summary of the lecture and frames environmental cancer risk in the context of personal decision-making.
